paper_contract.statement: Under the displayed smoothness and gradient-dominance assumptions, an epsilon-gradient estimate needs Wasserstein gradient-flow time at least on the order (1/lambda) log(L/sqrt(lambda epsilon)).

quantifier_under_test: The necessary-time wording is universal over losses and conditional energies satisfying the assumptions and asymptotic as epsilon tends to zero.

counterexample.data: rho_0=delta_0, hence every initial particle y_0=0
counterexample.smoothness: d^2 ell/dy^2=1, and d ell/d theta=y is 1-Lipschitz
counterexample.curvature: U is 3-strongly convex and satisfies |grad U|^2=6U
counterexample.non_warm_start: delta_0 differs from the Gibbs target; W2=1/sqrt(3)
counterexample.contradiction: Both the initial oracle and exact target oracle are zero, so every positive epsilon is met at t=0 while the claimed scale diverges.

acceptance_criteria: Symbolically verify every smoothness, PL, oracle, and asymptotic statement.
Independently normalize the continuous target and integrate its exact gradient oracle.
Observe first-hit time zero over at least six decreasing tolerances while the claimed scale is positive and increasing.
Reject a theta=1 control at t=0 and independently recover a strictly positive first-hit time.
Exit nonzero on any certificate, raw-data, checker, or control mismatch.
